name: Bad Häring
kurzbeschreibung: Relaxation and wellness destination featuring a modern Erlebnis-Therme and the most beautiful Kurpark in Tirol.
beschreibung:
Overview

Bad Häring is a renowned spa municipality in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley in the Kufstein district, situated on a sunny, fog-free plateau at roughly 650 meters above sea level. Home to around 2,900 residents, the town nestles at the foot of the distinctive Mount Pölven massif between the towns of Wörgl and Kufstein. As Tyrol's first officially recognized health resort and unique sulfur spa, Bad Häring has undergone a remarkable evolution from a historic coal mining settlement into a premier center for health, rehabilitation, and gentle recreation. Beautifully landscaped spa parks and sweeping vistas over the Inn Valley characterize this peaceful alpine village.

History

The settlement originated during early Bavarian colonization and was first documented in 1180 as Hering. For nearly two centuries, village life was defined by underground mining: in 1766, miner Jakob Weindl discovered extensive deposits of pitch coal in the Lengauer Graben ravine. Generations of miners worked the subterranean seams until extraction became unprofitable in the mid-20th century. During exploratory exploratory drillings for new coal seams in 1951, drillers tapped into a rich sulfur mineral spring at a depth of almost 300 meters. The spring was officially recognized as a medicinal mineral source in 1953, launching the town's spa tourism. In 1965, the municipality was formally granted the title Bad. The Gothic parish church of Saint John the Baptist, featuring a 1506 red marble portal and a 51-meter steeple, stands as a testament to the community's rich spiritual heritage.

How to Get There

By car, Bad Häring is reached via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Wörgl-Ost or Kufstein-Süd/Kirchbichl. From Kirchbichl, regional road L211 leads four kilometers up to the plateau in less than ten minutes. Rail travelers arrive at Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, an important ICE, Railjet, and Eurocity junction, or Kirchbichl regional station. Frequent VVT bus lines 4056 and 4902 provide direct connections to the village center and medical spa centers.

Tips

Health and wellness guests can relax at the Vivea Health Hotel or stroll through the landscaped spa gardens featuring an outdoor sulfur spring fountain and sensory barefoot path. The town's industrial legacy comes alive along the 5-kilometer Miners' Trail (Knappenweg), highlighted by information panels and historical tunnel portals, and at the local mining museum. Hikers enjoy circling the Pölven massif or ascending the Großer Pölven peak at 1,595 meters. In summer, the Plafing solar-heated outdoor swimming pool offers family recreation with panoramic mountain views.
